significance: The principal Shakta temple of Pokhara, established around the 1760s and given a royally appointed priest by King Girvan Yuddha Bikram Shah in 1815. Its hilltop compound also holds shrines to Saraswati, Shiva, Hanuman and Ganesha.
story: The goddess is held to be Yogamaya of the Vindhya hills in India, brought to Pokhara by royal order after a king's pilgrimage vision.
